problem.text: The author reports partial success with local CUDA installation, a log-artifact obstacle to multiple builds, and Python 3.13.4 issues. The diff narrows the build matrix and requests Python 3.13.3; it does not repair artifact handling.

reasoning.text: Commenting out selected configurations is a retry-oriented workaround rather than a general build-system repair. The Python pin and matrix reduction affect different selections; neither supplies a source-visible precondition for the other.

impact.text: The remaining configurations are Ubuntu Python 3.11, 3.12 and 3.13.3, plus Windows Python 3.13.3. No active non-CUDA packaging row remains.

source_notes.text: Read ancestor entries ae04741 and b2c3cab. They establish the workflow's introduction, non-isolated build preparation and Linux installer history; neither records a defect directly repaired by this change.

The supplied PR #13 evidence concerns conversion without a BOS token: oobabooga reports the failure, async0x42 reports another affected model, and turboderp thanks the contributor. It does not substantiate this workflow change's reported build success.

Closed issue #43, “Error converting abliterated Qwen3 mlabonne/Qwen3-30B-A3B-abliterated,” concerns invalid conversion states. Closed issue #16, “RuntimeError: CUDA error: invalid configuration argument,” ultimately discusses tokenizer truncation. Neither discussion establishes a connection to the matrix reduction or Python patch-version pin.

limitations: No GitHub Actions job, interpreter installation, CUDA provisioning or wheel build was executed. Successful completed wheels and the reported Python 3.13.4 problem remain unverified.
The inspected workflow has no explicit log-artifact upload. External action internals and any artifact-name collision are unestablished.
The Python computation models matrix edits using text processing; it does not execute YAML, PowerShell or GitHub Actions.

chapters.title: Narrow retry builds and pin Python 3.13.3

claims.text: Five rows become comments: Ubuntu Python 3.10, Windows Python 3.10–3.12, and the Ubuntu non-CUDA sdist row. The build steps themselves remain present, but the sdist branch has no remaining matrix configuration satisfying its empty-CUDA condition.

Both Python 3.13 rows change to 3.13.3. In this workflow matrix.pyver feeds the job display name and setup-uv's python-version input, so the edit requests a specific interpreter patch release rather than changing CUDA or Torch. Whole-parent search also finds matrix.pyver in calibration text, not another active workflow consumer.

All remaining rows retain CUDA 12.8.1, Torch 2.7.0 and the existing compilation-target list. Linux still selects cuda-toolkit v0.2.24 with method local and --toolkit; Windows retains its separately assembled toolkit. This commit does not introduce local installation.

Deleting the NVIDIA repository and exact-version package workaround removes already-commented text, not an active guard or installation step. The parent already performed local Linux toolkit installation without that workaround.

A bounded standard-library transcription counted nine parent matrix rows, five disabled rows and four remaining rows, reproducing the surviving OS/Python combinations. Four rows still remain, so this is not a conversion to one configuration per run.

Release publication remains conditional on release='1' and a parsed package version, selecting ./dist/*.whl. Whole-parent artifact search finds an upload-artifact example in calibration data but no explicit upload-artifact step in this workflow; the reported log-artifact problem cannot be localized to inspected workflow code.

annotation.summary: Disables five build configurations, pins remaining Python 3.13 builds to 3.13.3, and removes inactive CUDA workaround comments; build success remains unverified.

argv:
from pathlib import Path
import re
s=Path('.github/workflows/build.yml').read_text()
rows=[l for l in s.splitlines() if l.lstrip().startswith('- { artname:')]
removed=[l for l in rows if "artname: 'sdist'" in l or ("pyver: '3.10'" in l) or ("windows-2022" in l and any("pyver: '%s'"%v in l for v in ['3.11','3.12']))]
after=[l.replace("pyver: '3.13'","pyver: '3.13.3'") for l in rows if l not in removed]
print({'parent_rows':len(rows),'disabled_rows':len(removed),'remaining_rows':len(after)})
for l in after: print(l.strip())
